items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the state law, in relation to designating service dogs as the official state dog

approvalMessage.text:
APPROVAL MEMORANDUM - No. 26 Chapter 571

       MEMORANDUM filed with Assembly Bill Number 2756, entitled:

    "AN  ACT  to amend the state law, in relation to designating service
        dogs as the official state dog"

    APPROVED

  This bill would make the "service dog" the official dog  of  New  York
State.  A  service dog is defined in Agriculture and Markets Law Section
108 as any dog that has been or is being individually trained to do work
or perform tasks for the benefit of a person with a disability.

  During conversations with the  bill's  sponsors,  however,  it  became
clear  that  the  intent of the bill was not only to honor service dogs,
but also to recognize current and former "working dogs" that support and
assist New York's first responders, veterans, and civilians.

  Every day, working dogs protect, comfort, and  give  their  friendship
and  affection  to  New  Yorkers  in  need  of assistance. These devoted
companions embody the spirit of New York --  hard  working,  loyal,  and
eager to serve.

  The Legislature has agreed to a chapter amendment that would designate
the  working  dog as the official State dog. On that basis, I am signing
this bill.

  This bill is approved.                      (signed) ANDREW M. CUOMO

                                ______
